content.user_title: Analyze Software Issues with Root Cause Review
content.value_statement: Software issue reports often lack enough evidence for a clear fix. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through staged root cause analysis.
actual_capabilities: Collects symptoms, environment details, error messages, and reproduction steps.
Coordinates problem analysis, code investigation, and root cause validation stages.
Decides when recent-change analysis or log analysis should run.
Reviews Git history when a recent regression is suspected.
Analyzes logs, stack traces, and error patterns when provided.
Produces a final report with evidence, fix guidance, and validation steps.
limitations: Requires enough issue context to form useful hypotheses.
Depends on compatible agent or task support for named analysis roles.
Does not apply code fixes by itself.
Cannot inspect private logs or repositories unless access is available in the workspace.

use_cases.title: Triage Customer Bugs
use_cases.description: Turn a customer or PM report into missing questions, severity, and likely technical causes.

use_cases.title: Debug Recent Regressions
use_cases.description: Compare symptoms with recent code changes and rank suspicious commits or modules.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Alerts
use_cases.description: Connect logs, stack traces, and code paths into a root cause report with validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Bug Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use issue-review to analyze this bug report: [paste report]. Identify missing information, issue type, severity, and likely causes.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Recent Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Use issue-review for a recent regression. The issue began after [release or change]. Review likely code areas and recent changes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Logs and Stack Traces
prompt_templates.prompt: Use issue-review with these logs and symptoms: [paste logs]. Connect error patterns to code paths and root cause hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Root Cause Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full issue-review workflow for this incident: [context]. Include problem analysis, code investigation, optional Git or log review, root cause, fix guidance, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A PM reports that users cannot complete checkout in production.
output_examples.output: A triage summary names the symptom, missing data, likely causes, severity, and whether Git or log analysis should run.

output_examples.input: A deploy caused checkout failures after a payment dependency update.
output: Likely root cause candidates ranked by evidence.
Relevant files, suspect changes, and affected flow areas.
Recommended fix direction and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Server logs show repeated timeout errors for one API endpoint.
output_examples.output: A structured incident report links log signals to likely code paths and lists the next verification steps.

best_practices: Provide symptoms, environment, timestamps, expected behavior, and actual behavior.
Include relevant logs, stack traces, and recent release or change context.
Ask for evidence, confidence, and validation steps before implementing a fix.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for root cause analysis with only a vague phrase like it is broken.
Do not paste secrets, tokens, or customer personal data in logs.
Do not treat hypotheses as confirmed before code and evidence review.

faq.question: Does this skill fix bugs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It produces analysis, likely causes, fix guidance, and validation steps. A developer still applies and tests the fix.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Detailed symptoms, reproduction steps, environment data, timestamps, logs, stack traces, and recent change context work best.

faq.question: When should Git history analysis run?
faq.answer: Use it when the issue started recently, appeared after a release, or may be linked to a dependency or configuration change.

faq.question: Can it analyze production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure an incident review when you provide symptoms, logs, affected services, and available code context.

faq.question: Does it require logs?
faq.answer: No. Logs improve confidence, but the workflow can still analyze symptoms, reproduction steps, and code paths.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, but named agent behavior depends on the active environment.
